summary: Error Per Circuit Layer (EPCL) is an overlap-based circuit-level benchmarking protocol that estimates effective layer polarization by measuring the overlap between output states of two identically evolved quantum registers, avoiding classical simulation of ideal distributions. Numerical simulations validate EPCL under depolarizing and coherent noise while identifying sensitivity to register covariance and coherent entangling-layer errors, and hardware demonstrations on IBM Berlin show clear exponential decay in 8- and 16-qubit implementations.
motivation: Existing circuit-level benchmarks like mirror randomized benchmarking and cross-entropy benchmarking face scalability limitations: randomized benchmarking requires costly compilation for large systems, cross-entropy benchmarking requires classically simulated ideal output probabilities that become intractable at scale, and error per layered gate subsystem decomposition may miss correlated errors across multiple qubits.
method: EPCL applies identical random circuit layers (alternating Haar-random single-qubit gates and fixed two-qubit entangling gates) to two disjoint $n$-qubit registers and directly measures the overlap $\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_A \rho_B)$ between their noisy output states using either controlled-SWAP or Bell-basis measurements, fitting the depth-dependent decay to extract effective polarization $p_{\mathrm{eff}} = (p_A p_B)^m$.
result: EPCL recovers theoretical predictions under weak local stochastic noise ($\varepsilon_1 = 10^{-4}$, $\varepsilon_2 = 10^{-3}$ yield $\hat{p}_{\mathrm{eff}} = 0.99601$ versus first-order prediction $p_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\mathrm{FO}} = 0.99599$) and maintains single-exponential decay up to $\varepsilon_2 = 10^{-1}$; hardware on IBM Berlin demonstrates clear exponential overlap decay for $N=8$ (two 4-qubit registers, $p_{\mathrm{eff}} = 0.98190 \pm 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$) and $N=16$ (two 8-qubit registers, $p_{\mathrm{eff}} = 0.8949 \pm 3.0 \times 10^{-3}$).
